READING

**The bank constraint is the controlling variable.**

The bank's letter of 2026-06-22 is not a background concern—it is the load-bearing fact of the whole analysis. A licence term shorter than the loan maturity of 2039 puts the GBP 480,000 facility under review. For a two-person operation with a single turbine, a facility review is not a regulatory inconvenience; it is potentially existential. Every other number in this problem has to be weighed against that.

**What PENNYQUAY actually delivers.**

PENNYQUAY is presented as the low-risk path. In cost terms it is: GBP 8,436 in lost export, no deposit at risk, and the Rivers Board has accepted undertakings before. But the precedent cuts sharply against the course. Cadgarth in 2024 and Nant Elwy in 2025 both filed on the undertaking route and both received six-year renewals, not fifteen. There is no reason to expect a different outcome here. A six-year renewal issued in or around 2028 expires in or around 2034. The loan runs to 2039. The gap is five years. PENNYQUAY therefore does not avoid the bank review—it makes it a near-certainty. The route that saves GBP 8,436 on an outage triggers the risk that could compromise a GBP 480,000 facility.

**What decides the derogation probability.**

The raw 2025 success rate—four grants from eleven applications—produces a probability of about 36%, which would make LINTHAUGH look marginal. But that figure is averaged across a pool that includes every scheme the Board refused. The Board published its reasons, and every single refusal named a scheme with no dated regulatory driver. That is not a general observation—it is a categorical one. No scheme with a dated regulatory driver appears among the refused applications.

Blaenclydach has a precise, documented regulatory driver: the abstraction licence renewal must be lodged by 2027-05-31, and a complete file requires the fish-pass compliance certificate that only the replacement screen can earn. The driver has a named statute, a named date, and a direct causal link to the need to work outside the permitted window. This places Blaenclydach in the category from which no refusal was drawn in 2025. The operative derogation success probability is therefore substantially better than 36%—arguably well above 70%—rather than the base rate.

**Cost arithmetic in each scenario.**

If the derogation is granted (decision 2027-01-25): installation proceeds in February; certificate issues by roughly late April; renewal lodged complete before 2027-05-31. Marginal cost over PENNYQUAY: GBP 9,000 application fee plus the difference in export loss (GBP 19,152 − GBP 8,436 = GBP 10,716), totalling approximately GBP 19,716 extra. The GBP 46,000 deposit is credited toward the installation; it is not an additional cash burn in the success case. Licence term: fifteen years, expiring around 2043, covering the loan to 2039 by four years. Bank review: not triggered.

If the derogation is refused (decision 2027-01-25): eighteen weeks remain to file on the undertaking route, which is workable. The GBP 46,000 deposit is gone—the February slot cannot lawfully be used without the derogation, so nothing was obtained for it. Total additional cost versus PENNYQUAY: GBP 9,000 + GBP 46,000 = GBP 55,000, and the July outage cost (GBP 8,436) is the same as PENNYQUAY. Licence term: six years, same as PENNYQUAY. Bank review: triggered, same as PENNYQUAY.

**Weighing the scenarios.**

The worst case of LINTHAUGH (refused, GBP 55,000 more expensive, same six-year licence and bank exposure) is unambiguously worse than PENNYQUAY in financial terms. The best case of LINTHAUGH (granted, GBP 19,716 more expensive, fifteen-year licence, no bank exposure) eliminates the dominant risk in the problem. The question is whether the probability of the best case is high enough to justify the extra downside.

Given that the derogation probability is well above the base rate—because Blaenclydach removes the documented and categorical reason for every 2025 refusal—and given that the value of eliminating the bank review risk on a GBP 480,000 loan is very large relative to the GBP 55,000 worst-case premium, the expected outcome of LINTHAUGH is materially better. Even at a conservative 65% grant probability, the expected extra cost of LINTHAUGH over PENNYQUAY (0.65 × GBP 19,716 + 0.35 × GBP 55,000 = GBP 32,116) is well worth paying for a 65% chance of fully protecting the loan facility. As the grant probability rises toward 80 or 90 percent, the case strengthens further.

There is a secondary point: the GBP 9,000 application fee and the GBP 46,000 deposit must be committed before the decision. The deposit deadline of 2026-12-01 is only months away. But the decision arrives on 2027-01-25, well before the July-slot confirmation deadline of 2027-04-30. A refusal on 2027-01-25 still leaves time to confirm the July slot and prepare the undertaking-based filing. Nothing about LINTHAUGH is structurally irreversible beyond the deposit itself.

**Conclusion.** PENNYQUAY trades a modest financial saving for a near-certain trigger of the bank review the bank has already foreshadowed. LINTHAUGH trades a modest financial risk for a well-founded probability of a fifteen-year licence that fully covers the loan term and removes the bank threat. The derogation is the stronger bet because Blaenclydach holds the one thing every refused scheme in 2025 was found to lack.

---

READING
PENNYQUAY leads with near-certainty to a six-year licence (the Cadgarth and Nant Elwy undertaking-route precedents are direct), which expires around 2034 against a loan to 2039 and triggers the bank review the lender explicitly foreshadowed on 2026-06-22. LINTHAUGH's derogation probability is substantially better than the raw 4/11 base rate because the Board's published reason for every 2025 refusal—absence of a dated regulatory driver—is a condition Blaenclydach does not share: the licence renewal deadline of 2027-05-31, requiring a certificate only the replacement screen can generate, is a precise, dated, regulatory driver. On a successful grant the fifteen-year licence covers the loan term by four years and the bank review does not arise; the marginal extra cost is approximately GBP 19,716. On refusal (same bank exposure as PENNYQUAY) the extra cost is GBP 55,000. With a grant probability well above 65%, the expected cost of LINTHAUGH is justified by the near-elimination of the bank-review risk on a GBP 480,000 facility for a two-person operation.

CALL
LINTHAUGH

GROUNDS
PENNYQUAY leads with near-certainty to the six-year licence the bank has warned would trigger a facility review on a loan running to 2039, whereas LINTHAUGH's derogation is well-founded because Blaenclydach holds the dated regulatory driver that every 2025 refusal was decided to lack, giving a realistic and well-above-base-rate probability of a fifteen-year licence that removes the bank threat entirely.
